full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.196 of 1996 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka stating, inter-alia, that the late Mr. Batu Khan predecessors of the petitioner took lease of land measuring 1248 Ajutangsha from the Jaminder by paying proper salami and after his death his three sons Moti Khan, Hira Khan and Chunnu Khan become 16 (sixteen) anas owner of the suit property and thereafter of the permanent settlement of the suit land and on prayer Jaminder executed registered Kabulatnama in favour of Moti Khan, on 22.5.1907 as the said Moti Khan got Kabuliyat in respect of the suit property in his name, he and his two brothers namely Hira Khan, and Chunnu Khan, were also owning and possessing the same as per their share as inherited. During the C.S. operation the suit land was recorded in the name of Moti Khan, from the above three brothers. Hira Khan died leaving behind Lal kha as son and two daughters Paribanu, and Rehela died after the death of Hira Khan while they were unmarried. Chunnu Khan died leaving behind one wife Badrunnessa, three daughters namely, Hasan Banu, Bilkish Banu and Alder Banu, Akther Banu daughter of Badrunnessa, died unmarried leaving behind her two nieces Hasan Banu, Bilkish Banu as her heirs and uncle Moti Khan, her Hira Lal Khan only son of Hira Khasn had married Sakhina Banu and started living in that house in suit land. Sakhina Banu gave birth to Lal Khan's four legitimate sons and 5 daughters. Lal Khan died on 1943 leaving them behind as heirs. The recorded owner Moti Khan aged about 90, died unmarried and leaving Lal Khan son of Hira Khan, Hossain Banu and Bilkish Banu heirs of her brother Chunnu Khan as heirs to his left off properties Chunnu Khan gave marriage of his daughter Bilkish Banu with Bacchu Miah during his life. Arzoo Miah was the only legitimate son of Bacchu Miah, Bacchu Miah took charge of the family of late Chunnu Khan as he died without any son. Heirs of Chunnu Khan and Kim Khan for their convenience constructed semi puma house proportioning the 1248 Ajutangsha suit property among them. Among the 4 sons of Lal Khan, the plaintiff No, 2 is still alive and his 5 daughters have been living with their husbands. Sakhina died later.
